blocks.text: In Tiny Quest Deck, one person is the Game Master (the GM). The GM tells a story and plays all the monsters and characters you meet. Everyone else is a Hero. Together, you go on adventures, solve problems, and fight monsters.
The GM describes what's happening. The Heroes say what they want to do. When something is hard or risky, you roll dice to see what happens.

blocks.title: What you need to play
body: One d20 (the big 20-sided die) and one d6 (regular 6-sided die)
A pencil and a character sheet for each player
This rulebook (the Game Master uses it)

blocks.text: Every hero has three numbers that say what they're good at:

rows: Lift a gate, swing a sword
Cast a spell, solve a riddle
Sneak past a guard, shoot a bow

blocks.text: Your stat is a small number like +1, +2, or +3. You add it to your dice roll.

sections.title: The Main Rule: Roll a d20

blocks.text: When you try to do something hard, roll the d20 and add the stat that fits. If your total is 10 or more, you succeed!

blocks.title: Example
body: Lila the Knight wants to push open a stuck door.
Lila has Might +3. She rolls the d20 and gets a 9.
9 + 3 = 12. That's 10 or more, so the door creaks open!

blocks.text: Natural 20s and Natural 1s
If your d20 lands on 20 (before adding your stat), something extra cool happens. See the Legendary Roll table in the GM section.
If your d20 lands on 1 (before adding your stat), something goes funnily wrong. See the Legendary Fail table in the GM section.
When you fight a monster, take turns going around the table. On your turn:

items: Move (you can always move a little bit, no roll needed).
Do ONE thing: attack, cast a spell, or help a friend.

blocks.text: Some powers are marked Reaction or Free Action — those don't use up your one thing (see Quick Rule Words).
Attacking

Roll the d20 and add the right stat (Might for heavy weapons, Mind for spells and magic weapons, Speed for light weapons and bows). If your total is 10 or more, you hit! Then roll the d6 and add your stat — that's how much damage the monster takes.
Getting Hurt
Every hero has a Max HP (Health Points) that comes from their class and their armor. When you get hit, the GM tells you how much damage you take. Cross off that many HP boxes on your character sheet.

blocks.title: You don't die
body: If your HP hits 0, you're knocked out. A friend can heal you to wake you up. You don't die — Tiny Quest Deck is a friendly game.

blocks.text: Tiny Quest Deck powers come back in two different ways. This keeps big signature moves special while letting everyday tricks fire more often.

rows: You take a break after a tough fight or a long stretch. All HP comes back, all spells come back, and powers marked (Rest) recharge.

Roll a d6 at the start of your turn. On a 6, all (Recharge) abilities and non-rest spells come back. Roll only during combat. On a recharge you may also swap one Ready Spell for one from your Spellbook, for free.

blocks.text: These are the words that show up on cards, in spells, and in monster quirks. The first four (Hurt, Stuck, Frightened, Asleep) are conditions — they plug into team combos.

rows: Wounded, burning, poisoned, sick, or weakened. Roll with −1 until it ends.
Cannot move for the listed time. You can still attack or cast spells if you can reach.
Scared or shaken. Roll with −1 and you can't move toward the thing that scared you until it ends.
You are knocked out. You cannot do anything. A friend can wake you by shaking you (uses their turn) or by hitting you for 1 damage.
A bonus move. It does not use your normal turn.
Use during another player's or an enemy's turn. Once per round.
A break. Used spells and many powers come back. Some signature abilities only recharge with a rest and are marked (Rest).

Roll a d6 at the start of your turn. A 6 recharges all (Recharge) abilities and non-rest spells. Roll only during combat. On a recharge you may swap a Ready Spell for one from your Spellbook, for free.
Enemies do not target you. Usually ends when you attack. Scout-only.
Roll d20 to hit as a free action for dual wielding. Damage is d6 only.

blocks.text: Heroes get stronger as the adventure goes on. Each class levels the same way:

rows: Base HP goes up (add gear bonuses). Boost your stats by 2 points (all on one stat, or split them). Gain your Path Power.
Base HP goes up again. Boost your stats by 2 more points. Gain your Path Signature powers.

blocks.title: In the app
body: Tap your level badge on the character sheet to level up — spend your 2 points across Might, Speed, and Mind however you like. Your new powers appear automatically.

blocks.text: Any character can use any gear. Pick the weapon and armor that fit your hero's style! Each weapon belongs to a category that decides which stat you roll to hit.
Weapon Categories

blocks.title: Light weapons vary
body: Some light melee weapons hit with Might (heavier one-handers like maces and hand-axes) and some with Speed (finesse blades like daggers and rapiers). The app shows the exact stat for each weapon when you add it — that's the source of truth.

blocks.text: Armor
Armor makes tracking health easy by directly increasing your Max HP.

rows: Uses one hand. Cannot use Bows or Heavy Melee.

blocks.text: This section is for the Game Master. Keep it handy while you run the game — it covers how to decide what to roll, how hard things are, and how monsters work.

sections.title: What Stat Should I Call For?

rows: Push, lift, smash, climb a rope
Swing a sword, axe, or club
Resist being knocked over or poisoned
Cast a spell, recall a fact, solve a puzzle
Talk to an animal or a magical creature
See through an illusion or trick
Shoot a bow or throw something
Pick a lock, balance, do a tricky climb

blocks.text: By default, a roll of 10 or more succeeds. If something is harder than usual, raise the target. If it's easier, skip the roll entirely.

rows: Walking across a room, opening an unlocked door
Climbing a slick wall, sneaking past a watchful guard
Lifting a portcullis alone, fooling a dragon

blocks.text: Legendary Roll (natural 20)
When a hero rolls a natural 20, they deal max dice damage, then double it. After damage is applied, they pick one:

blocks.title: Option 1 — Shockwave
body: Knock down enemies around the target and give them Stuck. Plus, ask the GM to alter the room in a small way:
The struck target flies into the boss and knocks an item out of its hand.

blocks.title: Option 2 — Free Action
body: Take an extra free action right away.

blocks.title: Why it's fun
body: Instead of just doing math, the kid gets to describe an epic moment: “I chop his shield in half so he can't block,” or “I shoot my arrow so hard it pins him to the wall and he's Stuck.” You just say “Yes” to whatever they describe.

blocks.text: Legendary Fail (natural 1)
When a hero rolls a natural 1, something goes funnily wrong. Keep it light — the goal is laughs, not ruined plans.

rows: You accidentally hit an ally with the attack instead (you pick which one).
You do the opposite of what you were trying to do.

blocks.text: Pick monsters to fit the scene. Most have HP between 4 and 20. To attack a hero, the monster rolls d20 + its To-Hit; on 10+, the hero takes the listed damage. Quirks make each monster memorable — use them!

rows: Cowardly. Runs if half its friends fall.
Hunts in pairs. Gives one bite, then circles.
Falls apart on a natural 20 against it.
Hit hero is Stuck until they roll Might 10+.
Will surrender if outnumbered or scared.
On hit, hero is Hurt for 2 rounds.
Slow. Heroes go first. Loves to brag.
Sneezes (everyone in front: d6 fire) on a 1.
Steals one item. Leaves a flower in its place.

blocks.text: Quick Monster Math
If you need to invent a monster on the fly, use these rules of thumb:

After a good fight or a clever solution, hand out a reward. Gear, gold, a funny item, or a new spell all work. Let the treasure fit the story — a defeated wizard drops a wand; a dragon's hoard has gold and a magic sword.

blocks.title: In the app
body: Heroes track Normal Items and Magic Items right on the character sheet. Add whatever you award — the app keeps the list. Gear that changes stats (weapons, armor) goes in the Gear box and updates Max HP automatically.
